free_tier.stated: No free tier is documented: a third-party review checked in October 2026 states that search and downloads require an active subscription, and a comparison table lists NZBGeek's free tier as 'None (subscription required)'. An unkeyed search is refused with an empty-API-key error and caps declares registration available=no. Earlier third-party readings of a free trial and of a few downloads a day are not found on the pages read now. The public site lists no prices.
free_tier.notes: The conservative reading is the one the vendor's own API supports: an unkeyed call is refused, and no reading of the free tier describes an API allowance enough to drive an arr stack. The 5-calls-a-day figure is unsourced, not contradicted.

per_object_cap.stated: not applicable: an NZB pointer file

retention.stated: not stated on the API surface. A third-party listing claims 'NZBs from 8 years ago available, 500,000+ indexed NZBs' (nzbhydra.com, 2026-10-23).

egress.terms: No byte metering: the API returns XML pointers. The payload is served by whichever news provider a user pays.

interface_detail: Newznab API on a separate host, api.nzbgeek.info/api, not nzbgeek.info/api (the apex returns HTML). caps declares <limits max="100" default="100"/> and <registration available="no" open="no"/>. An unkeyed search returns error code 102.
tooling: Native Newznab: Prowlarr, NZBHydra2, Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr and Mylar all add it with URL plus key. No wrapper needed. The API host is different from the site host, which is the first mistake a hand-rolled config makes.
chaining: A broad, well-populated index that a paid arr stack reaches with no wrapper; on the free tier it contributes nothing to automation, because no reading of the free tier gives an API allowance that could drive a stack.

limits.value: no free API allowance that a stack can use; paid membership USD 12/year

limits_note: The 100 is a per-request result ceiling and applies to every tier; it is not the paid allowance.
binding_note: The API call allowance is what fails first: without a key the first automated search is refused outright (error 102), and the readings of the free tier that describe an allowance put it at 5 calls a day, which is one search every five hours.

identity_cost.detail: Registration is contradictory at the vendor: the login page links 'register account?' and register.php serves a Registration Agreement with an 'agree' submit, while /api?t=caps declares <registration available="no" open="no"/>; a third-party review checked in October 2026 states that registration was open. The fields a signup demands are unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: The membership is what keeps the index alive; a lapsed membership drops the account back to the capped tier and automation stops with no partial service.
confidence_note: The caps and the unkeyed error were measured. Creating one free account and reading its API page would move this to documented.

unkeyed search returned 200 with 47 bytes: <error code="102" description="Empty API Key"/>, so the API is closed to a free, unauthenticated caller
the apex host serves HTML for /api, 91,943 bytes; the API lives only on api.nzbgeek.info
an anonymous GET receives the Registration Agreement plus an 'agree' submit, which contradicts the caps registration flag; no POST was made

third-party: the paid tier 'removes download caps and unlocks full API integration'
third-party: 'NZBgeek used to have a free level, but now you need a paid membership to search and download.'
a 2026 third-party review: search and downloads require an active subscription

notes: Two vendor signals contradict each other on registration: a served agreement form says open, caps says available=no. The conservative reading is recorded on the record and not resolved, because resolving it needs an account. The verdict rests on the API allowance, which is independent of that question.
